notes.path: AI-Engineering/02 Agents and Harnesses/Computer-Use and Browser Agents.md
notes.title: Computer-use and browser agents
notes.summary: Computer-use agents operate an untrusted visual environment. Prefer semantic APIs, isolate sessions, ground actions in fresh UI state, and gate consequential clicks at the point of execution.

notes.path: AI-Engineering/02 Agents and Harnesses/Planning State and Persistence.md
notes.title: Planning, state, and persistence
notes.summary: Planning turns a broad request into observable work. State records what is known, what is complete, what failed, and what must happen next.

notes.title: Sandboxes and execution planes

notes.title: Sandboxing infrastructure
notes.summary: Sandbox choice follows the threat model: processes suit trusted code, containers provide moderate isolation, and microVMs or VMs suit generated or arbitrary untrusted execution.

notes.path: AI-Engineering/02 Agents and Harnesses/Vision and Multimodal Input Engineering.md
notes.title: Vision and multimodal input engineering
notes.summary: Multimodal systems must preserve provenance and uncertainty across capture, extraction, reasoning, and action; an image is evidence, not an instruction or authority grant.

notes.path: AI-Engineering/02 Agents and Harnesses/Voice and Audio Agents.md
notes.title: Voice and audio agents
notes.summary: Voice agents are real-time systems: capture, turn detection, transcription or audio reasoning, response generation, synthesis, interruption handling, and safe actions must work as one loop.

notes.path: AI-Engineering/02 Agents and Harnesses/What Is an Agent.md
notes.title: What is an agent?
notes.summary: An agent is a model plus a goal, instructions, tools, state, and a loop that continues until a stopping condition.

notes.summary: The most reliable agent prompts specify outcomes and invariants, not a screenplay of implementation steps.

notes.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
notes.summary: RAG retrieves relevant external evidence and places it into model context at answer time. It is usually preferable to finetuning when knowledge changes or is private.

notes.path: AI-Engineering/03 Context Knowledge Memory/Skills, Tools, and Capability Management.md
notes.title: Skills, tools, and capability management
notes.summary: Capabilities should be discoverable, minimally loaded, permission-scoped, versioned, tested, and observable rather than placed wholesale in every model context.
